units.headline: New benchmark for filterSeriesAndSortPostings across input fractions
units.summary: Adds a benchmark that measures filterSeriesAndSortPostings with the isSeriesWithoutOOO predicate over 100k head series at varying input fractions. Test-only code, so a line-by-line review can be skipped.

risk_signals: package-level mutable test hook in production code
units.reason: Test hook that stays nil in production; it only runs when a test sets it.
units.headline: Adds a testing hook that runs before head-view eviction
units.summary: Adds a package-level func var that compactHeadViewLocked calls between writing blocks and evicting series. It is nil unless a test sets it, so production behavior does not change.

units.reason: New shared compaction and eviction path that decides when head series are dropped; mistakes lose data.
units.headline: Shared head-view compaction loop with an append-ID watermark for eviction
units.summary: Pulls the per-chunk-range block write, reload and evict loop out of CompactStaleHead into a helper that CompactStaleHead and the new CompactSelectedSeries both use. It captures committedAppendID before writing so that series which got later commits are not evicted, skips reloads for empty views, and builds a fresh BlockMeta for each range.
focus: committedAppendID returns a low watermark (all IDs at or below it committed) and returns 0 when isolation is disabled
maxt is read before the watermark is captured; check that gcSeries skips series whose samples are newer than maxt
if reloadBlocks fails on a later chunk range, blocks from earlier ranges stay loaded while their series remain in the head
the inclusive maxt in truncateSeries together with the inclusive loop bound

issues.title: Watermark comment overstates the block guarantee for samples newer than maxt
issues.failure_scenario: An appender commits a sample at ts > maxt after maxt is read but before committedAppendID() runs. Its appendID is at or below the watermark, but the loop stops at maxt, so no block holds that sample. Eviction is safe only if gcSeries rejects series with samples newer than maxt.
issues.detail: The comment promises that every sample at or below the watermark is in a block. That does not hold for samples timestamped after the captured maxt. The safety then rests on the maxt check in gcSeries.

issues.title: Reload failure on a later range leaves earlier blocks overlapping the head
issues.failure_scenario: Range 1 writes and reloads a block, then range 2's reloadBlocks fails. Only range 2's uids are removed and the function returns before evict. Range 1's block stays loaded while the same series and samples remain in the head, so the data is duplicated and overlapping.
issues.detail: The cleanup only deletes the current iteration's blocks. This logic was moved from CompactStaleHead.

units.headline: Renames staleIndex to selectedSeriesIndex with renamed reader types

risk_signals: new selection path for series eviction
units.reason: Generalizes series selection with a caller predicate run under the series lock; it now drives which series the new public API evicts.
units.headline: Generic ref filter with predicate replaces stale-only series selection
units.summary: Replaces the stale-only selection loop with a generic filter that resolves postings to head series and applies an optional keep predicate under the series lock. It returns refs in input order and in label order. CompactStaleHead and CompactSelectedSeries both use it.
focus: sortedByRef keeps the input order, so callers must pass sorted, duplicate-free postings (CompactSelectedSeries sorts and compacts)
with a nil keep, series are read without taking the lock

units.reason: Clearly equivalent refactor: same AllPostings input and the same OOO-and-stale check under the series lock.
units.headline: staleSeriesRefsNoOOOData now delegates to filterSeriesAndSortPostings
units.summary: Re-implements the stale-series lookup as a call to filterSeriesAndSortPostings with an isSeriesWithoutOOO && isStaleSeries predicate. That matches the old inline checks run under the same lock, so the result is unchanged.
